title: Get a marriage license
question: How do we get a marriage license in Charlottesville?
office: Clerk of the Charlottesville Circuit Court (constitutional officer)
summary: Any Virginia circuit court clerk issues marriage licenses; in Charlottesville, the Circuit Court Clerk's Office, 315 East High Street. Both people come together, Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm (arrive by 4:15), bring government photo ID, complete the application at the office kiosk and swear to it. The fee is $30 (cash, check or money order): a $20 state tax plus a $10 clerk fee. Both must be 18; there is no residency requirement, waiting period or blood test. The ceremony must take place in Virginia within 60 days, and the officiant returns the certificate to the clerk within five days. Certified copies come from the clerk (copy fee not published) or the state Office of Vital Records ($15 a copy).

steps.step: Check that you can marry in Virginia
steps.who: Both people who plan to marry
steps.how: Both of you must be at least 18. Neither may still be married to someone else (that marriage must be ended first), and Virginia bars marriage between an ancestor and descendant, between siblings (half or whole blood, or by adoption), and between an uncle or aunt and a nephew or niece. The clerk may not refuse a license because of the couple's sex, gender or race. A divorced person need not wait after the divorce and need not bring the decree.
steps.quote: The minimum age at which persons may marry shall be 18.

steps.step: Line up an authorized officiant and a wedding date within 60 days of getting the license
steps.how: The ceremony must be performed in Virginia by someone the law authorizes: a minister authorized by an order of a circuit court, its judge or its clerk (Va. Code § 20-23); a judge, clerk or other official listed in § 20-25, who needs no order; or any other person who gets an order from a circuit court clerk under § 20-25 (the petitioner pays $25 to record it, and the clerk may require a $500 bond). A person authorized under § 20-25 may charge no more than $75 for the ceremony, plus travel expenses (additional services may be negotiated), and must give you the cost of the ceremony and travel at least three days before the ceremony (§ 20-27). A religious society with no ordained minister may marry its members by its own practice; one person the society chooses completes the certificate and must give a $500 bond with surety (§ 20-26). Clergy and religious organizations acting in their religious capacity may refuse to perform any marriage (§ 20-13.2). The Charlottesville Clerk's Office does not perform ceremonies or keep a list of civil officiants; its page refers couples without an officiant to the Charlottesville Sheriff's Office (434-970-3777), whose page lists a ceremony cost of $50. Do not get the license until the wedding is within 60 days.
steps.deadline: Marry within 60 days of the date the license is issued
steps.fee: Officiant's fee, if any; the Sheriff's Office lists $50 for a ceremony. Recording a clerk's order authorizing a person to officiate (§ 20-25): $25, paid by the petitioner.
steps.quote: Our office does not provide "Justice of the Peace" services at the Courthouse for immediate unions nor maintain a list of "Civil Officiants".

steps.step: Gather photo ID and the information the application asks for
steps.how: Each of you should bring a valid, unexpired government photo ID (driver's license, passport or DMV ID card). The application asks each of you for: full name; address; age and date of birth; place of birth (state or foreign country); which number marriage this is (first, second, third and so on); marital status if previously married (widowed or divorced); education (highest grade completed); and both parents' names (first, middle and maiden or last). State law also requires each person's social security number, or a DMV control number, and signature on the application. You may list yourselves as spouse, bride or groom. No blood test is required, and a divorced person does not need a copy of the divorce decree.
steps.quote: Both parties should have a valid, non-expired government-issued photo ID such as a driver’s license, passport, or DMV issued ID card to present upon request.

steps.step: Apply together, in person, at the Charlottesville Circuit Court Clerk's Office and swear to the application
steps.who: Both people, present together; Clerk's Office staff (clerk or deputy clerk)
steps.how: Go to the Clerk's Office at 315 East High Street, on the lower level of the Circuit Courthouse (the Sheriff's page gives the office as 315-C East High Street), Monday to Friday between 8:30 am and 4:30 pm. Both of you must be there at the same time; there is a special process when one person is incarcerated (ask the Clerk's Office). You fill in the application at the office's marriage computer kiosk, which takes about 10 to 15 minutes; a staff member then reviews it and gives you the required oath. A false statement on the application can be prosecuted as perjury. No appointment is mentioned. You do not have to live in Charlottesville or in Virginia; any Virginia circuit court clerk can issue the license.
steps.deadline: Monday through Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm; plan to arrive by 4:15 pm
steps.quote: Both parties need to be simultaneously present when the application is made although there is a special process available when one of the parties is incarcerated.

steps.step: Pay the $30 fee and receive the license and two certificate copies
steps.how: Pay $30 by cash, or by check or money order made payable to the City of Charlottesville Circuit Court (the page does not mention cards). The $30 is the $20 state license tax (of which $10 goes to services for victims of domestic violence) plus the clerk's $10 fee. The clerk gives you the license and two copies of the marriage certificate for your officiant to complete. There is no waiting period: you may marry as soon as the license is issued.
steps.quote: $30 fee payable by cash or check/money made payable to the City of Charlottesville Circuit Court.

steps.step: Hold the ceremony in Virginia within 60 days
steps.how: The license is good for a ceremony anywhere in Virginia for 60 days from the day it is issued. If the 60 days pass without a ceremony it expires, and you must apply again: a new license needs a new application that meets every requirement, and a new fee. An officiant who performs a ceremony without a valid license, or without authority, commits a crime; but a marriage made under a Virginia license is not void only because the officiant lacked authority or the license had a defect, if the marriage is otherwise lawful and either or both of the couple fully believed they were lawfully married (§ 20-31). The Sheriff's page says witnesses are not required for its ceremonies; no Code section requiring witnesses was found.
steps.deadline: Within 60 days from the date of issuance
steps.quote: Every marriage license issued under § 20-14 shall constitute authority for a period of only sixty days from the date of issuance for the solemnization of a marriage of the licensees.

steps.step: The officiant completes the certificate and returns it to the Charlottesville clerk
steps.how: After the ceremony the officiant certifies the facts of the marriage and files the record, in duplicate, with the clerk who issued the license (here the Charlottesville Circuit Court Clerk) within five days. The clerk keeps and indexes the original in the marriage register and sends the state's copy to the State Registrar of Vital Records by the tenth day of the next month. An officiant who does not comply faces a $25 penalty, and each year the clerk lists unreturned licenses for the Commonwealth's Attorney.
steps.deadline: Within five days after the ceremony
steps.quote: Every person who officiates at a marriage ceremony shall certify to the facts of marriage and file the record in duplicate with the officer who issued the marriage license within five days after the ceremony.

steps.step: Get certified copies of the marriage certificate
steps.who: Either spouse (or another person entitled to the record); Charlottesville Circuit Court Clerk's Office or the Virginia Department of Health, Office of Vital Records
steps.how: For a copy from the Circuit Court, call the Clerk's Office at 434-970-3766; the city's page gives no fee or procedure. The Office of Vital Records issues certified copies through its online system, by mail on Form VS6MD (a print-and-sign PDF, also in Spanish; include a legible copy of your ID), or in person at its Richmond lobby; its FAQ says most records are also available at local DMV or health department offices. Each certified copy, or a search when no copy is made, costs $15 (effective July 1, 2026); the FAQ says there is no refund if no record is found. Online requests are paid by credit card; mailed requests by check or money order payable to the State Health Department (no cash by mail); in-person requests by check, money order, card or cash. Standard processing takes about two weeks; express delivery is offered. The clerk may also give you a commemorative certificate (§ 20-16), which is not a certified copy. Until 25 years after the marriage, Vital Records issues marriage records only to immediate family (spouse, parents, children, siblings, grandparents) with valid ID.
steps.fee: $15 for each certified copy (or search) from the Office of Vital Records; the Clerk's Office copy fee is not stated on the city's pages
steps.quote: the $15.00 fee rate will apply to each certified copy of a vital record that is issued, or for each search of the system of vital records where a certified copy of a vital record is not made.

caveats: No Charlottesville City Code section governs marriage licenses; state law sets the requirements, fee and validity, and the clerk's page describes office practice. The City Code (published on Municode, whose terms are not confirmed to allow reuse) is not quoted. The two local legal_basis entries are office procedures from the city's court page, not ordinances.
The 'special process' for when one person is incarcerated is mentioned on the city page but not described there, and no Virginia Code section on it was found in the index. Ask the Clerk's Office.

The marriage license application is completed on the Clerk's Office kiosk on a form the State Registrar furnishes (Va. Code § 32.1-267(E)). No downloadable application or online pre-application for Charlottesville was found, so none is listed in forms.

The ID requirement ('should have ... to present upon request') is office practice on the city page; no Code section requiring photo ID was found. The SSN or DMV control number requirement comes from Va. Code § 32.1-267(B); the city page's list of required information does not mention it.
The city page says the fee is payable by 'cash or check/money' (apparently meaning check or money order); card payment is not mentioned, so whether cards are accepted is unconfirmed.

The Sheriff's page says 'The Code of Virginia provides that the Sheriff may perform a wedding ceremony.' No section naming sheriffs was found: § 20-25 lists judges, clerks and certain officials who need no order, and sheriffs are not among them, so the Sheriff's officiants probably act under a § 20-25 clerk's order. This was not confirmed. The page names the two officers who perform ceremonies; their names are left out here. The $50 ceremony cost is within the $75 cap in § 20-27, if that section applies.

Whether a refused applicant can get mandamus against the clerk is a legal judgment. Title 20 gives no appeal from a refusal; the only express fallback is the judge's power in § 20-14 when the clerk and deputies cannot act. The mandamus rungs rest on the general procedure in §§ 8.01-644 and 8.01-645, the venue rule in § 8.01-261(5), and on issuance being a clerk's duty under §§ 20-14 and 20-13.2. Applying to another circuit court clerk is the practical alternative.

The Clerk's Office fee for copies or certified copies of a marriage record is not published on the city's pages (the Request Copies page says to call 434-970-3766). Va. Code § 17.1-275(A)(8) and (A)(9) set general copy ($0.50 a page) and certificate ($2) fees, but whether the clerk applies them to marriage certificates was not confirmed.

The Office of Vital Records fee rose to $15 on July 1, 2026 (VDH notice citing Chapter 616 of the 2026 Acts of Assembly). The index text of Va. Code § 32.1-273 (cap of $15) matches. Because clerks forward marriage records to the State Registrar monthly (§ 32.1-267(D)), a state certified copy may not be available right after the wedding; that is an inference, not something either office states.

Applications and registers that show social security or control numbers are not open to general public inspection (§ 32.1-267(F)); the license itself remains public. Vital Records releases marriage records only to immediate family until 25 years after the event (VDH page).

The city page and the vacourts.gov page name the Clerk of Court and the judges, and the vacourts.gov page gives the Clerk's personal mailbox. Only office channels are recorded here. No general office mailbox for marriage licenses was found.

The city page does not say whether appointments are needed or whether walk-ins are served until 4:30 pm; it says to arrive by 4:15 pm. The Sheriff's page gives the Clerk's Office as 315-C East High Street; the court page gives 315 East High St.

State-law quotes are matched to Open US Law's copy of the Code of Virginia; some keep that copy's spacing before punctuation (for example '§ 20-25 , $25'). Section text has not been compared with the live law.lis.virginia.gov pages.

Vital Records payment methods differ by channel. The main page's drop-off option lists check, money order, payment card, mobile pay or cash; the FAQ says online requests are paid by credit card, mailed requests by check or money order (no cash by mail), and in-person requests by check, money order, all major credit cards or cash. Form VS6MD (English and Spanish) has no fillable fields; the forms page lists it among PDF forms to print at home.

'One-time officiant order' is not § 20-25's wording (an order may authorize 'one or more persons' and is rescindable); now 'a clerk's order authorizing a person to officiate', here and in the fee row. Added the § 20-27 duty to give the cost and travel at least three days before the ceremony, the § 20-26 requirement that the society's chosen person completes the certificate and gives a $500 bond with surety, and the § 20-13.2 right of clergy to refuse.

Step s8: the $15 also covers a search when no copy is made (VDH notice, § 32.1-273(A)); added the FAQ's no-refund rule, payment by channel (online by card; mail by check or money order, no cash; in person by check, money order, card or cash), the two-week standard processing time, and the § 20-16 commemorative certificate. The rung on record errors now attributes the 'Vital Records corrects only birth and death records' point to the VDH FAQ.
Summary: the $15 figure applied to both sources of copies; now $15 a copy from Vital Records, with the clerk's copy fee unpublished.

The Clerk's Office fee for copies or certified copies of a marriage record is unpublished (Request Copies page says to call); the § 17.1-275(A)(8)-(9) amounts are not confirmed as applied.

The Sheriff's page says the Code lets the Sheriff perform weddings, but no section naming sheriffs was found in the index (§ 20-25 does not list them); the Sheriff's officiants probably act under a § 20-25 order. The $50 cost is the office's published figure.
